headline: The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,244 for a second straight session as Meta's Muse assistant kept the AI chip trade running, while a fifth day of falling crude on US Iran talks took WTI down 5.91 percent to 90.12 dollars and let the rupee firm to 95.62.

summary.us: The Nasdaq Composite added 0.45 percent to a record close of 27,244 on 22 September while the S&P 500 finished flat at 7,765 and the Dow fell 185 points to 51,864, as AI infrastructure names offset weakness in banks and energy. The 10 year Treasury yield held near 4.97 percent with traders waiting on about ten Fed speaker appearances this week, and JPMorgan gave back roughly 3 percent a day after disclosing a 20 billion dollar partnership with the Qatar Investment Authority.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed at 23,329 and the Sensex fell about 330 points on 22 September, with the Nifty IT index down around 1.5 percent after CLSA flagged muted discretionary demand and EPS downside risk at Infosys and Wipro. Foreign investors sold 3,810 crore rupees of cash equities against 4,120 crore rupees of domestic institutional buying, while the rupee gained 16 paise to 95.62 as Brent eased toward 99 dollars.
summary.global: Tokyo stayed shut for a five day Silver Week break that leaves the Nikkei 225 at its 18 September close of 65,018.95 with trading due to resume on 24 September, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng edged up 0.18 percent to 25,088. European markets were mixed as the DAX added 0.10 percent to 25,600 and the FTSE 100 slipped 0.29 percent to 10,708, with energy names lagging after Brent settled near 99 dollars and copper held within 1 percent of its record on emptying Shanghai and London warehouses.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
